name: Lammas

attributes.attribute: the English name for the feast of Lughnasa
harvest festival of the first of August
goddess honored by the feast's athletic contests

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lammas is the English name for the Celtic feast of Lughnasa. Lughnasa was the harvest festival of the first of August and one of the four great feasts of the Celtic year. The feast took its name from the god Lugh. Some say Lugh created it in honor of his mother, the goddess Tailtiu, who died on that day. Athletic contests were held in her name. Among the continental Celts, Lughnasa was the time of the great Council of the Gauls. The feast closed the year's cycle, for the next great feast, Samhain, marked the beginning of the new year. Lammas thus points the reader to the greater feast of Lughnasa.

okr.objective: Present Lammas as the English name for the Celtic harvest feast of Lughnasa.
key_results: State that Lammas names the feast of Lughnasa on the first of August.
Note the feast's link to the god Lugh and the goddess Tailtiu.
Mention Samhain as the following feast that opened the new year.
